speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a chronic cough and have had recurrent bouts of bronchitis. To understand the underlying cause, how long has your cough been persisting, and do you smoke or have any other known exposures to irritants?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual duration of symptoms for typical chronic bronchitis, especially in a non-smoker. Can you tell me if you have any shortness of breath, wheezing, or a history of allergic rhinitis or sinus issues? Also, does the sputum production improve or worsen with seasonal changes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of copious, thick, yellow-green sputum for 11 years in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia or Kartagener syndrome. Have you experienced recurrent sinus infections, chronic nasal congestion, or situs inversus (reversal of internal organs) in the past? Please also describe any episodes of abdominal pain or infertility, as these are associated with this condition. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
